Answer a remark the way a lackadaisical teenager would, depending on whether it is a question, a shout, both, or silence.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/bob) (MIT). Listed under [Strings & Text](/examples/?subject=strings-and-text).

```nomi-run
// FILE: bob.nomi
//# Bob, a lackadaisical teenager, and how he answers what is said to him.

/// Bob's reply to `remark`. He answers a question, a shout, a shouted
/// question and silence each in his own way, and anything else with
/// "Whatever."
pub fn response(remark: String) -> String {
    remark = String.trim(remark)
    if remark == "" { return "Fine. Be that way!" }

    case #(String.ends_with(remark, "?"), String.is_upper(remark)) {
        #(True, True) -> "Calm down, I know what I'm doing!"
        #(True, False) -> "Sure."
        #(False, True) -> "Whoa, chill out!"
        #(False, False) -> "Whatever."
    }
}

// FILE: bob_test.nomi
import bob.response

test "bob's responses" {
    cases = [
        #("asking a question", "Does this cryogenic chamber make me look fat?", "Sure."),
        #("shouting", "WATCH OUT!", "Whoa, chill out!"),
        #("forceful question", "WHAT'S GOING ON?", "Calm down, I know what I'm doing!"),
        #("silence", "", "Fine. Be that way!"),
        #("stating something", "Tom-ay-to, tom-aaaah-to.", "Whatever."),
        #("asking a numeric question", "You are, what, like 15?", "Sure."),
        #("asking gibberish", "fffbbcbeab?", "Sure."),
        #("question with no letters", "4?", "Sure."),
        #("non-letters with question", ":) ?", "Sure."),
        #("prattling on", "Wait! Hang on. Are you going to be OK?", "Sure."),
        #("ending with whitespace", "Okay if like my  spacebar  quite a bit?   ", "Sure."),
        #("multiple line question", "\nDoes this cryogenic chamber make\n me look fat?", "Sure."),
        #("shouting gibberish", "FCECDFCAAB", "Whoa, chill out!"),
        #(
            "shouting a statement containing a question mark",
            "DO LIONS EAT PEOPLE? AHHHHH.",
            "Whoa, chill out!",
        ),
        #("shouting numbers", "1, 2, 3 GO!", "Whoa, chill out!"),
        #(
            "shouting with special characters",
            "ZOMG THE %^*@#$(*^ ZOMBIES ARE COMING!!11!!1!",
            "Whoa, chill out!",
        ),
        #("shouting with no exclamation mark", "I HATE THE DENTIST", "Whoa, chill out!"),
        #("prolonged silence", "          ", "Fine. Be that way!"),
        #("alternate silence", "\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t", "Fine. Be that way!"),
        #("other whitespace", "\n\r \t", "Fine. Be that way!"),
        #("talking forcefully", "Hi there!", "Whatever."),
        #(
            "using acronyms in regular speech",
            "It's OK if you don't want to go work for NASA.",
            "Whatever.",
        ),
        #("no letters", "1, 2, 3", "Whatever."),
        #("statement containing question mark", "Ending with ? means a question.", "Whatever."),
        #("starting with whitespace", "         hmmmmmmm...", "Whatever."),
        #(
            "non-question ending with whitespace",
            "This is a statement ending with whitespace      ",
            "Whatever.",
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, remark, expected), description {
        assert response(remark) == expected
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- Silence leaves early with `if remark == "" { return ... }`, and the other
  four answers are a `case` on the tuple `#(question, shouting)` with all four
  Bool pairs written out. The checker proves the four arms exhaustive, and the
  table reads as the problem's rules. A chain of `else if`s was the
  alternative.
- A shout is `String.is_upper(remark)`: the remark has a letter, and every
  letter is upper case. That is the problem's rule in one call. Comparing the
  remark with `String.uppercase` of it was the alternative, but `"1, 2, 3"`
  equals its own upper case, so that needs a second check for a letter.
- The parameter is trimmed into a binding of the same name
  (`remark = String.trim(remark)`), per style §11.
- Replies are plain Strings, since the canonical data compares strings and
  nothing else consumes them.
- The "other whitespace" case writes its remark `"\n\r \t"`, the escapes the
  canonical data uses, so the test reads as the specification does.
- The case "multiple line question" (uuid 66953780) is left out because
  canonical data replaces it with uuid 2c7278ac, which is included under the
  same description.
